name: Morpheus8 Burst

card.summary: The deeper Burst-mode RF microneedling setting of InMode's Morpheus8; little independent evidence exists for it specifically.
card.note: Evidence is thin and largely industry-linked.

quick.overview:
Morpheus8 Burst is the Burst-mode, deeper-reaching configuration of InMode's RF microneedling device, marketed for tightening skin and mild fat reduction.

Specific published research is minimal; one registered trial looked at multi-depth RF microneedling for cellulite.
quick.mechanism: Insulated needles penetrate the skin and release RF energy at chosen depths, heating tissue to prompt collagen remodeling.
quick.risks: Redness, swelling and pinpoint bleeding are common; burns, scarring, infection and pigment changes are described as rarer risks.

lead: Morpheus8 Burst refers to the Burst mode and deeper attachments of the Morpheus8 radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system from InMode, which uses insulated microneedles to deliver bipolar RF energy into the dermis and subdermal tissue.[1] It is used to tighten loose skin, smooth texture and scarring, and contour small areas of the face and body, so the appearance payoff is firmer-looking skin and a sharper jawline or neck without surgery.[1][3]

Radiofrequency microneedling combines the collagen-stimulating effect of microneedling with deeper heating from RF energy. A 2019 review described its indications as skin rejuvenation, acne scarring, laxity and hyperhidrosis, and said treatment parameters need optimising for safety and efficacy.[3]

Published work on the Morpheus8 platform includes a multicenter retrospective study of 247 patients combining bipolar RF with Morpheus8 for lower face and neck laxity, in which Baker face and neck classification improved by an average of 1.4 points and 93 percent said they were pleased.[3] Evidence specific to the Burst mode is minimal; the registered trial matching this entry tested multi-depth RF microneedling for cellulite.[2]

chain: Insulated needles deliver RF energy at chosen depths
Heating prompts collagen remodeling and tissue contraction
Firmer skin, smoother texture and tighter jaw and neck contour
angle.text: Morpheus8 sessions aim to tighten skin and soften lax areas, including the lower face and neck, by combining microneedling with RF heat. Deeper Burst-mode attachments are marketed for body areas and subdermal tissue.

infobox: Standard tips and Burst deep-body attachment[1]
Skin laxity, lower face and neck, texture, cellulite[3][2]

paras: An AI-generated encyclopedia entry describes Morpheus8 as delivering bipolar RF through insulated needles in Burst mode, with tips ranging from superficial resurfacing pins to deeper subdermal tips and a Burst deep-body attachment, and treatment depths adjustable from 0.5 to 8 mm.[1] That account is untrusted and not independently verified. Published surgical literature describes Morpheus8 as a modification of the Fractora fractional RF device, used alone or combined with bipolar RF devices such as FaceTite and BodyTite.[3]

A 2019 supplement in Aesthetic Surgery Journal describing combined adjustable-depth fractional RF with bipolar RF for skin laxity and adipose remodeling was based on the authors' clinical experience, who reported it as effective and safe; the record lists a grant from InMode.[3] A 2020 multicenter retrospective study of 247 patients (mean age 55.1) found the Baker classification improved by 1.4 points on average, with the authors concluding the approach may fill a gap but does not replace a facelift or necklift.[3] Grokipedia states that many Morpheus8 studies are industry-sponsored and independent data beyond 12 months is limited.[1]

A 48-person registered study evaluated RF microneedling with multi-depth targeting per insertion for cellulite of the leg.[2] The 247-patient retrospective study and a 2019 clinician-experience report cover Morpheus8 combined with bipolar RF,[3] and a 2019 review covers RF microneedling generally.[3] No studies specific to the Burst mode were identified.

In the 247-patient study, prolonged swelling beyond six weeks occurred in 4.8 percent, a hardened area over 12 weeks in 3.2 percent, and marginal mandibular neuropraxia in 1.2 percent, all resolving without intervention.[3] The Grokipedia entry lists temporary redness, swelling and pinpoint bleeding as common effects and burns, scarring, infection and pigment changes as rarer risks, and states the FDA has flagged risks of RF microneedling devices.[1] A 2019 review said multiple studies support minimal risk, including in darker skin types.[3]

timeline.event: Reviews and clinician reports describe Morpheus8 combined with bipolar RF for skin laxity.[3]
Multicenter retrospective study of 247 patients with lower face and neck laxity is published.[3]
FDA soft-tissue contraction clearance reported for Morpheus8.[1]
